purpose: Teach: コマース/押し出し/平米/弐/作製/一任/隔週/通りかかっ

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、Eコマース詐欺の捜査もご担当ですね
lines.en: Police handle e-commerce fraud investigations too, don't they?
lines.style: Curious, genuinely interested tone. Leaning in slightly with a question that invites explanation. Warm and open—not interrogating, just wanting to understand what they do.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、容疑者を一気に押し出した制圧も訓練されますね
lines.en: You must train constantly for those suspect-apprehension drills—the controlled takedowns, right?
lines.style: Impressed, almost admiring. A slight rise on the recognition of physical difficulty. Steady pace, genuine respect underneath the conversational tone.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、犯行現場の平米数を計測されますね
lines.en: And you actually measure out crime scenes by the square meter—that precision work falls to you?
lines.style: Noting the meticulous detail with mild wonder. Light emphasis on the specificity of it. Conversational but clearly struck by the exactness.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、書類に弐の漢数字を厳密に使われますね
lines.en: I've noticed you use the formal kanji character for 'two' on official documents—it's that strict, isn't it?
lines.style: Observant, slightly playful observation. A small knowing smile in the voice—he's noticed a detail others might miss. Warm, not mocking.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、お尋ね者ポスターの作製も担当されますね
lines.en: Creating wanted posters, that comes under your department's work too?
lines.style: Matter-of-fact acknowledgment with a touch of curiosity. Straightforward question, no judgment. Continuing the thread of understanding their responsibilities.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、専門部署に一任する事案もありますね
lines.en: Though there are cases you hand off to the specialist divisions, I imagine?
lines.style: Knowing and pragmatic. A slight nod in the voice—understanding that not everything is handled in-house. Collaborative tone, no edge.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、隔週で地域防犯ミーティングを開かれますね
lines.en: You hold those biweekly community safety meetings in the neighborhood, don't you?
lines.style: Acknowledging community-facing work with understated respect. Conversational but warm—recognizing that this kind of preventive outreach matters.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、犯行現場をたまたま通りかかった目撃者の証言を重視されますね
lines.en: And you really do put a lot of weight on the testimony of witnesses who happen to pass by a crime scene, don't you?
lines.style: Leaning in closer now, tone shifts slightly to more intimate observation. A real question underneath—probing gently at how much those chance sightings actually matter. Kenji's genuine interest surfaces here.
